newsitem.title: USA: Celgene gets patent for new SelCIDs.
newsitem.headline: Celgene gets patent for new SelCIDs.

text.p: Celgene Corp said Tuesday that it had been awarded a patent for composition of matter for new additions to the SelCID (Selective Cytokine Inhibitory Drugs) family of novel compounds developed by Celgene.
According to Celgene, the SelCIDs have been shown to be potent inhibitors of a destructive immune response, the chronic overproduction of tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-alpha).

"The new patent further strengthens our proprietary position on a highly promising family of novel compounds, which are being evaluated for their potential for treating rheumatoid arthritis, asthma, inflammatory bowel disease, multiple sclerosis, and other prevalent inflammatory diseases," said John Jackson, chairman and chief executive officer, in a press release.
The first of these SelCID compounds is expected to enter initial clinical trials later in 1997, the company said.
